chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Had the pilgrim known what rewards await him from the carriers (mounts), no one would consider a camel to be expensive.

key_terms.الْحُمْلَانِ: al-humlan — riding on mounts, specifically the reward/merit accruing to one who rides a mount during hajj
key_terms.غَالَ بِبَعِيرٍ: to consider a camel expensive/to overpay for a camel

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for riding a camel or mount during the Hajj pilgrimage in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) encourages pilgrims performing the hajj to value their riding mounts generously by revealing the immense spiritual reward attached to the act of riding mounts during the pilgrimage. The hadith highlights that if pilgrims truly understood the divine recompense awaiting them for riding mounts (al-humlan) on the way to Mecca, they would never hesitate to pay any price for a camel. This teaching encourages readiness to invest in the means of fulfilling the hajj obligation by connecting worldly expenditure to otherworldly reward.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Had the Pilgrim known what is for him from the carriers, no one would consider the camel to be expensive’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Had the pilgrim to Makkah known what carries his load, camel would not become expensive.’”
